name: Cytoscape.js + React ref wrapper
summary: The primary Cytoscape.js path in a real React component: the core API owns a ref-mounted container, with a React 19 wrapper and no stale react-cytoscapejs dependency. The 20-node/20-edge spike rendered, selected a node and mounted in 25 ms.
gains: Works with React 18 and 19 through a thin ref wrapper
No dependency on the stale react-cytoscapejs package
Selection and graph interaction available through the core API
losses: The application owns the wrapper lifecycle and cleanup
No built-in editor, stencil or history layer
Layout extensions are separate packages with their own maintenance
Bundle includes React and Cytoscape: 640.68 KB / 204.31 KB gzip in the spike
Canvas rendering is slower than WebGL for very large graphs

spike.scenario: 20 nodes, 20 edges, Cytoscape 3.34.4 mounted from a React 19.2.0 ref wrapper, grid layout, node selection, Vite production build, 1200x800 Chrome screenshot.
spike.notes: The spike uses the Cytoscape core API directly from a React component, not react-cytoscapejs. A node selection succeeded through the core instance. The bundle includes React 19.2.0; Cytoscape's own 138 KB gzip figure is the library-only cost.
